stem.en: One of these ancestors made handaxes and cleavers, and was the first hominin to leave Africa. Which one?

image.alt: Four fossil hominin skull casts in a row, labelled Homo habilis, Homo erectus, Homo neanderthalensis and Homo sapiens from left to right.

text.en: Homo habilis, because it made early stone tools.

feedback.en: Homo habilis made simple choppers and is known from Africa. The handaxes and the first journey out belong to its successor.

text.en: Homo sapiens, because modern humans went everywhere first.

feedback.en: Homo sapiens left Africa much later, around 125,000 years ago, and it made more complex tools.

text.en: Homo neanderthalensis, because it lived in Europe.

feedback.en: Neanderthals lived in Europe and southwest Asia, but they made flake tools and were not the first hominins to leave Africa.

explanation.en: Homo erectus invented handaxes and cleavers and began to leave Africa about 2 million years ago. Homo sapiens left much later, around 125,000 years ago.

hints.en: Think of the tool first: which ancestor is linked with handaxes and cleavers?
